problem: Find $c$ such that the average value of $f(x)=-3\sqrt{x}$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $-6.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Average Value of a Function

feedback.problem:
In **ascending order**, the **exact** nonzero values of $c$ such that the average value of $f(x)=12{x}^{2}-16x-12$ over the interval with endpoints $0$ and $c$ is equal to $0$ are

$c=$
{{field-1}} $\,$ and  $\,c=$
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
To solve for $c\ne 0,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{ave}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 0 & =\frac{1}{c-0}{\int }_{0}^{c}(12{x}^{2}-16x-12)\,\text{d}x \\ 0 & ={\frac{1}{c}(4{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}-12x)|}_{0}^{c} \\ 0 & =\frac{1}{c}[(4{c}^{3}-8{c}^{2}-12c)-0] \\ 0 & =4{c}^{2}-8c-12 \\ 0 & =4({c}^{2}-2c-3) \\ 0 & =4(c-3)(c+1) \\ c & =-1,\,3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in **ascending order**, the values of $c$ are 

$$
c=-1\,\text{and}\,c=3.
$$
